claim_limit: 模型生成假设、选择登记候选并修改代码；计分及实验后阈值决策为确定性内核。单轮公开数据开发验证，不证明创新或通用自主科研能力。
implementation_verification_note: 逐 seed 改动语句覆盖通过；同进程轨迹并非对抗证明，也不证明改变影响预测或科学机制成立。

alternatives: GaussianNB may match or exceed random forest if the diagnostic classes are well described by independent Gaussian feature distributions.
A depth-6 forest may underfit complex boundaries or overfit noisy labels, reducing accuracy relative to GaussianNB.
Class imbalance or insufficient samples per class could favor the simpler GaussianNB baseline.
candidates.applicability: Applies to the fixed public split with diagnostic labels, the registered n_estimators=200 and max_depth=6 configuration, same label definitions and evaluation protocol; no claim of clinical validity.
falsification: If random_forest(n_estimators=200, max_depth=6) accuracy is less than or equal to GaussianNB accuracy on the fixed split, the hypothesis is falsified.
If the accuracy difference is zero or negative under the same evaluation protocol, the hypothesis is falsified.
candidates.mechanism: Hypothesis: random_forest with n_estimators=200 and max_depth=6 will achieve higher diagnostic-label accuracy than GaussianNB on the fixed split because tree ensembles can model non-linearities and feature interactions without assuming Gaussian class-conditional distributions or feature independence.
predictions: random_forest(n_estimators=200, max_depth=6) test accuracy on the fixed split will be greater than GaussianNB test accuracy.
The accuracy difference (random_forest minus GaussianNB) will be positive on the fixed split.

alternatives: GaussianNB may match or exceed SVC if the class-conditional feature distributions are approximately independent and Gaussian.
RBF-SVC results depend strongly on feature scaling and C=2.0; poor scaling or an unsuitable C could erase any advantage.
Sample size, class overlap, or label noise may make the simpler GaussianNB baseline competitive or better.
candidates.applicability: Applies to the fixed public split with diagnostic labels, numeric features in a representation suitable for an RBF kernel, the registered C=2.0 configuration, and consistent preprocessing; it tests integration behavior only.
falsification: If svc_rbf(C=2.0) accuracy is less than or equal to GaussianNB accuracy on the fixed split, the hypothesis is falsified.
If the accuracy difference is zero or negative under the same evaluation protocol, the hypothesis is falsified.
candidates.mechanism: Hypothesis: svc_rbf with C=2.0 will achieve higher diagnostic-label accuracy than GaussianNB on the fixed split because the RBF kernel induces a flexible non-linear decision boundary and margin-based optimization can separate classes that are not linearly separable and not well modeled by independent Gaussian features.
predictions: svc_rbf(C=2.0) test accuracy on the fixed split will be greater than GaussianNB test accuracy.
The accuracy difference (svc_rbf minus GaussianNB) will be positive on the fixed split.

alternatives: GaussianNB may match or exceed extra trees if the diagnostic classes follow approximately independent Gaussian distributions.
Randomized split selection and max_depth=8 may underfit or overfit depending on sample size and noise, removing any ensemble advantage.
Class imbalance, irrelevant features, or label noise could favor the simpler GaussianNB baseline.
candidates.applicability: Applies to the fixed public split with diagnostic labels, the registered n_estimators=200 and max_depth=8 configuration, same evaluation protocol and label definitions; not a medical validation.
falsification: If extra_trees(n_estimators=200, max_depth=8) accuracy is less than or equal to GaussianNB accuracy on the fixed split, the hypothesis is falsified.
If the accuracy difference is zero or negative under the same evaluation protocol, the hypothesis is falsified.
candidates.mechanism: Hypothesis: extra_trees with n_estimators=200 and max_depth=8 will achieve higher diagnostic-label accuracy than GaussianNB on the fixed split because extremely randomized tree ensembles can capture non-linear feature interactions and are less dependent on Gaussian and independence assumptions.
predictions: extra_trees(n_estimators=200, max_depth=8) test accuracy on the fixed split will be greater than GaussianNB test accuracy.
The accuracy difference (extra_trees minus GaussianNB) will be positive on the fixed split.

alternatives: GaussianNB may match or exceed logistic regression if features are approximately conditionally independent and Gaussian within each diagnostic class.
Preprocessing, class imbalance, label noise, or limited sample size could remove any linear-model advantage.
The true boundary may be non-linear, so a linear logistic model may underfit relative to GaussianNB in some class regions.
candidates.applicability: Applies to the fixed public data split with diagnostic labels, numeric or appropriately encoded features, no train/test leakage, and the registered C=1.0 configuration; this is an integration comparison, not a medical-effectiveness claim.
falsification: If logistic_regression(C=1.0) accuracy is less than or equal to GaussianNB accuracy on the fixed split, the hypothesis is falsified.
If the accuracy difference is zero or negative under the same evaluation protocol, the hypothesis is falsified.
candidates.mechanism: Hypothesis: on the fixed public split, logistic_regression with C=1.0 will achieve higher diagnostic-label accuracy than the GaussianNB baseline because its discriminative linear log-odds model does not impose conditional independence and can exploit correlated or non-Gaussian feature distributions when the decision boundary is approximately linear.
predictions: logistic_regression(C=1.0) test accuracy on the fixed split will be greater than GaussianNB test accuracy.
The accuracy difference (logistic_regression minus GaussianNB) will be positive on the same fixed split.
